chunks: The adhan and the iqama are dual (each sentence said twice). The obligations of the prayer are seven: the time, the purification, the tawajjuh, the qibla, the ruku', the sujud, and the supplication.

The qunut is in every prayer, obligatory and voluntary, in the second unit before the ruku' and after the recitation. It suffices for the saying in the qunut: "My Lord, forgive and have mercy, and overlook what You know, indeed You are the Most Powerful, the Most Generous."

And three glorifications (tasbihat) also suffice in it. And if the praying person wishes to mention the Imams (peace be upon them) in his qunut and to bless them, then let him mention them collectively.

key_terms.الأذان: Adhan: the call to prayer, each phrase repeated twice
key_terms.الإقامة: Iqama: the second call immediately before commencing prayer
key_terms.القنوت: Qunut: supplication made in the second unit of prayer, before bowing
key_terms.تسبيحات: Tasbihat: glorifications of God (subhan Allah, alhamdulillah, Allahu akbar)
key_terms.فرائض الصلاة: The obligatory pillars of the prayer, here enumerated as seven

ai.seo_question: What are the seven obligations of prayer in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This teaching from al-Amali of al-Shaykh al-Saduq outlines the fundamental obligations of salat according to Shia jurisprudence, enumerating seven pillars. It further details the qunut supplication -- its placement in the second unit, acceptable minimum wording, and the ruling on mentioning the Imams collectively rather than individually during qunut. This was recorded in a scholarly assembly (majlis) in 368 AH, reflecting the established jurisprudential teachings transmitted by Shia scholars of that era.
